value.behaviour: ColorPicker accepts an optional popupId that replaces `type` as its AppState.openPopup key, so several pickers of one palette type can coexist.
rules: 1. ColorPickerProps gains `popupId?: Extract<AppState["openPopup"], "textRangeColor" | "textRangeHighlight">;` with a JSDoc (the openPopup key this picker opens under; defaults to `type`).

2. ColorPickerComponent destructures popupId and derives `const popupKey = popupId ?? type;`; every `appState.openPopup === type`, `appState.openPopup !== type` and `updateData({ openPopup: type })` in ColorPickerComponent uses popupKey instead (TopPicks follow-focus, Popover open/onOpenChange, trigger toggle, popup-content condition).
3. ColorPickerPopupContent gets a `popupKey: NonNullable<AppState["openPopup"]>` prop and its onClose compares `getOpenPopup() === popupKey`; ColorPickerComponent passes popupKey.
4. isColorPickerPopup also returns true for "textRangeColor" and "textRangeHighlight"; its type predicate becomes `popup is ColorPickerType | "textRangeColor" | "textRangeHighlight"`.
5. ColorPickerTrigger gets a `popupKey` prop and uses it for data-openpopup; title logic stays keyed on `type`.
6. areColorPickerPropsEqual compares `prev.appState.openPopup === (prev.popupId ?? prev.type)` / same for next in the early return, and adds `prev.popupId === next.popupId` to the equality list.
7. With popupId absent, behaviour and rendered markup are exactly as today.

value.behaviour: While a text is edited, shifts its style ranges on every text change and keeps AppState.textEditorSelection in sync with the textarea selection; clears it on submit.
rules: 1. Add `import { shiftRangesForEdit, withStyleRanges } from "@excalidraw/element";` after the getWrappedTextLines import line.

2. Declare a local `const syncTextEditorSelection = () => { ... }` before `if (onChange) {`: if isDestroyed is true return; read start/end from editable.selectionStart/selectionEnd; build next = { elementId: element.id, start, end }; if app.state.textEditorSelection has the same three values return; else app.setState({ textEditorSelection: next }). (isDestroyed is declared later with `let`, so reference it only inside the function body.)

3. In editable.oninput, after normalization and BEFORE onChange(editable.value): read `const latest = app.scene.getElement(element.id)`; when it is a text element with non-empty styleRanges, compute `const next = withStyleRanges(latest, shiftRangesForEdit(latest.styleRanges, latest.originalText, editable.value))` and, when next !== latest, call `app.scene.mapElements((el) => (el.id === latest.id ? next : el))` (a new object, so the key is dropped when the list empties). Then call onChange as today (App.text.ts's updateElement spreads this latest element and sets the new originalText), then syncTextEditorSelection().

4. Register textarea listeners for "select", "keyup" and "mouseup" calling syncTextEditorSelection, and call it once after the initial selection is applied (after the autoSelect block); remove the three listeners in cleanup().
5. In handleSubmit, right after cleanup(), when app.state.textEditorSelection is not null call app.setState({ textEditorSelection: null }).
6. Use ownerDocument/ownerWindow only; no document/window globals in new code.
